key_insight: A high-Reynolds-number asymptotic analysis shows that free-stream forcing excites non-modal perturbations in hypersonic blunt-body boundary layers through a nose-region slow-down convection mechanism followed by downstream lift-up growth.
engineering_relevance: The reduced model helps predict receptivity-driven disturbance amplification in hypersonic boundary layers, which is important for transition control, thermal protection design, and sensitivity to nose radius or wall temperature.
method: High-Reynolds-number asymptotic theory for hypersonic blunt-body boundary layers
Identify key receptivity mechanisms near the stagnation region and downstream
Build a reduced model and compare it against SF-HLNS calculations
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the reduced-model predictions agree well with SF-HLNS simulations across the receptivity-driven downstream evolution.
watch_item: The model is asymptotic and mechanism-focused, so accuracy may degrade outside the high-Reynolds-number regime or when geometry/thermal conditions depart from the assumptions used in the analysis.
paper_title: Excitation of non-modal perturbations in hypersonic boundary layers by free stream forcing. Part II: asymptotic theory and key mechanisms
